clue.text: Throughout lap, I'm following

indicators.note: following says the I'm comes after the word for lap

parts.note: to lap a rival in a race is to pass them, so lap gives pass
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A runner overtaking someone on a lap, staying behind them all the way.
explanation.walkthrough: PASSIM is Latin, used in footnotes to mean a source is cited throughout a work.
explanation.definitionFit: Passim is a Latin footnote term meaning a reference occurs at many places throughout.

clue.text: Founder, as one punctures coastal feature

indicators.note: something that punctures goes into another thing, so ONE sits inside the coastal word

parts.note: a pier is a structure jutting out from the coast
taken as the word one

explanation.surface: Someone starting a seaside business as a pier is holed.
explanation.definitionFit: A founder of something new is a pioneer, the first to open up a field.

clue.text: Autopsy — no doctor's admitted body to see

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the answer is held inside the run of words Autopsy no doctor's

explanation.surface: A post-mortem where no doctor has been let in to look at the corpse.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; a synod is the governing assembly of a church district, so 'body to see' is a body attached to a see.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is a church council, the governing body serving a bishop's see or province.

clue.text: The smell of anger?

definitions.meaning: the fragrant smoke of burning spices in church
as a verb, to make someone furious, stressed on the second syllable

explanation.surface: Asking what fury smells like.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is perfumed smoke from burning resin; the verb, stressed differently, means to enrage someone.

clue.text: Criminal nicking first and sixth from another

indicators.note: nicking means stealing, so the first and sixth letters are taken away from the other criminal

parts.note: another criminal, here a smuggler

explanation.surface: One crook robbing another of a couple of things.
explanation.walkthrough: SMUGGLER loses its first letter S and sixth letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: A mugger is a street robber who attacks victims, a common kind of criminal.

clue.text: Caveman's comment's a bloomer in hideous manner

parts.note: ug is the grunt cartoon cavemen make
a lily is a flower, something that blooms

explanation.surface: A primitive man grunting about a mistake, in an ugly way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder (British slang for a mistake) but is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb formed from ugly describes doing something in a hideous, unattractive way.

clue.text: Bush harbours condition that's half Arab offered

indicators.note: harbours means shelters within, so the condition and half-word go inside the bush

parts.note: gorse is a spiny yellow-flowered shrub
if introduces a condition

indicators.note: half signals taking the first part of that, giving two letters

explanation.surface: A shrub sheltering a horse that's partly Arab bred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' looks like the American president but is a shrub. The proverb says never look a gift horse in the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arab is a breed of horse, and one offered for nothing is a gift horse.

clue.text: A further time, deliver book

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
to serve is to hand over or deliver, as with a writ or a ball

explanation.surface: Asking someone to deliver something again.
explanation.definitionFit: To book a table or seat is to reserve it in advance.

clue.text: Hurried to haul up into place restrictive practice

indicators.note: into says the hurried and hauling words go inside the place

parts.note: a station is a place or post
ran means hurried

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: to lug is to haul or drag

explanation.surface: Rushing to drag something into position as a limiting rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restrictive practice' is a British trade-union term for a rule limiting output, here read literally as choking.
explanation.definitionFit: Strangling restricts breathing, so it is literally a restrictive practice, a witty twist on the industrial phrase.

clue.text: See 15 and 19
Main thing saw Tory leader quite socialist, not centre

annotationWithheld.why: Main thing saw Tory leader quite socialist, not centre: parse is CUT + T (Tory leader) + LEFTISH less its centre T, but the check reads the T dropped and the separate Tory T as one moved letter (movedLetter) and refuses every honest form
annotationWithheld.clue: Main thing saw Tory leader quite socialist, not centre

clue.text: Novelist to unite by fusion?

definitions.meaning: to join metal on by melting, read as two words

explanation.surface: A writer joining things by heating them.
explanation.definitionFit: Fay Weldon was a British author; read as two words it means to attach by welding.

clue.text: No one here sane

definitions.meaning: nobody is present here because everyone is elsewhere

explanation.surface: Nobody in this place is of sound mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads the phrase literally: if no one is here, all are over there.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means mentally sound; literally it says everyone is in that other place.

clue.text: Boast about French team ahead of English many years ago

indicators.note: ahead of puts the first part before the English letter
about means around, so the boasting word surrounds the team

parts.note: brag means boast
onze is French for eleven, the size of a football team

explanation.surface: Bragging about a French side leading the English.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bronze Age was a prehistoric period thousands of years ago, when bronze tools were used.

clue.text: Atop note amid new or old coin, one coined specially

indicators.note: amid puts the atop and note words in the middle of new

parts.note: on means atop
C is a musical note
taken as written
d was the abbreviation for the old British penny

explanation.surface: A coin description with a note on top, one minted for the occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coined' in the definition means invented, not minted; 'old coin' is the pre-decimal British penny.
explanation.definitionFit: A word invented for one occasion only is said to be coined for that special use.

clue.text: Support turns in lower capital

indicators.note: in puts the turned support inside the word for lower

parts.note: to lower, rhyming with flower, is to scowl or frown

indicators.note: turns means the support word is read backwards

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: A support that turns in a lower position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' here rhymes with flower, an old word for scowl. FREETOWN is the capital of Sierra Leone.
explanation.definitionFit: Freetown is the capital city of Sierra Leone in West Africa.

clue.text: Bet the Euro's replaced it

definitions.meaning: the Irish currency superseded by the euro in 2002

explanation.surface: A gamble that the single currency has replaced a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A punt is a small bet, and also the former Irish pound, replaced by the euro.

clue.text: A few coppers strip

definitions.meaning: a paltry sum of money, coppers being small coins
a comic strip, the one featuring Charlie Brown

explanation.surface: A handful of police officers undressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' are low-value bronze coins in Britain, not police; 'strip' is a comic strip, not undressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Peanuts means a trivial amount of money, and it is Charles Schulz's famous comic strip.

clue.text: Nervous house losing five to plague

indicators.note: losing means the letter for five is dropped from the house

parts.note: a villa is a house
V is the Roman numeral for five
to tease is to pester or plague

explanation.surface: A household losing five members to a plague, all on edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ill at ease is uneasy, uncomfortable and nervous.

clue.text: Stately, a state capital

parts.note: august means stately, majestic

explanation.surface: A grand and dignified seat of state government.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusta is the capital of the US state of Maine.

clue.text: Team's broadcast contains what they do want and don't

indicators.note: contains means the broadcast word holds the other pieces

parts.note: sown means scattered, broadcast like seed
a team wants to win
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A team's broadcast includes what fans want and what they don't.
explanation.walkthrough: SWINDON TOWN is an English football club; 'broadcast' means scattered like seed, not televised.
explanation.definitionFit: Swindon Town is an English professional football team based in Wiltshire.

clue.text: Last four rounds pinching many stools behind bars

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet

indicators.note: pinching means gripping between, so the many letter goes inside the rounds

parts.note: four Os, each a round shape
D is the Roman numeral 500, many

explanation.surface: The final rounds of a bar crawl ending with stools in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stools' are droppings and 'behind bars' means in a cage, not seats in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoo doo is manure from zoo animals, the droppings of creatures kept in cages.

clue.text: Measure of toe wrestling, so conducted?

parts.note: a bar is a measure in music

indicators.note: wrestling suggests the letters of of toe being twisted about

explanation.surface: A bout of toe-wrestling, done with no shoes on.
explanation.walkthrough: OF TOE rearranged gives EFOOT. 'So conducted' refers back to toe wrestling, done with bare feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Toe wrestling is performed without shoes or socks, so it is conducted with bare feet.

clue.text: Plan contracted by a country

indicators.note: contracted means shortened, so the plan word loses its final letter

parts.note: a gambit is an opening plan or ploy

explanation.surface: A scheme agreed with a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gambia is a small West African country along the Gambia river.

clue.text: Menial work caught Jack among rabble

indicators.note: among means placed in the middle of the rabble

parts.note: a mob is a rabble
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
J is the abbreviation for jack in cards

explanation.surface: A labourer named Jack caught up in an unruly crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A McJob is slang for low-paid, unskilled employment with few prospects.

clue.text: The Guardian's about to cook food on the barbie?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the newspaper's word goes round the rest

parts.note: the newspaper is speaking of itself, so its word is ours
taken as written

indicators.note: to cook something up is to rearrange it, so food is shuffled

explanation.surface: A newspaper about to grill food on a barbecue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook' rearranges FOOD into FDOO. A barbie is Australian slang for a barbecue.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooking on a barbecue happens in the open air, outside the house.

clue.text: Wear green

explanation.surface: An instruction to dress in green.
explanation.definitionFit: Jade means to wear out or exhaust, and it is a green colour named after the stone.

clue.text: Relative to face Edison invention

indicators.note: invention suggests making something new out of the letters of the inventor's name

explanation.surface: A relation meeting the inventor Edison's latest creation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relative' looks like a family member but means in relation to.
explanation.definitionFit: Viewed from the side relative to the front face, an object is seen in profile.

clue.text: Element withdrawing support in party

indicators.note: in places the reversed support within the party

parts.note: Con is short for the Conservative party

indicators.note: withdrawing means drawing back, so the support word is read in reverse

parts.note: a bra is a supporting garment

explanation.surface: A member pulling back support within a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawing' turns BRA backwards to ARB; a bra is the support, not political backing.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbon is a chemical element, number six in the periodic table.
